name: Sitagliptin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Sitagliptin is a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor cleared by the kidneys. The US label lowers the dose to 50 mg daily at an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 30 to 44 and to 25 mg daily below 30 or on dialysis, without regard to dialysis timing.

bands.recommendation: 100 mg once daily; no adjustment (label: eGFR ≥45).
eGFR 45–59: 100 mg once daily. eGFR 30–44: 50 mg once daily (label).

hd.text: 25 mg once daily, without regard to dialysis timing (label).
hd.short: 25 mg daily, any time vs HD

dialyzable: Modestly: about 13.5% removed over a 3–4 hour hemodialysis session (label).
monitoring: Assess kidney function before starting and periodically (label). Pancreatitis, hypoglycemia with sulfonylureas or insulin.

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and effectiveness not established in pediatric patients; pediatric trials (10–17 years) did not show efficacy (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
